messages:
maria: Quick check-in — saw a couple of weird cases where stale cache keys get republished after a prefix handoff in prod-canary (03/18 08:12 UTC). 4 occurrences in 48h. Anyone running into this?
aj: saw one yesterday, assumed it was TTL hiccup. not confident.
kevin: digging through the handoff logs, there's a `republish` background task on demote. sample lines:
```
2026-03-18T08:12:14Z nodeA demote: start prefix=P epoch=42
2026-03-18T08:12:14Z nodeA republish: key=K1 ts=1711221134 epoch=41 trace=abc123
2026-03-18T08:12:14Z nodeB promote: accept prefix=P epoch=42
2026-03-18T08:12:15Z nodeB write: key=K1 ts=1711221140 epoch=42 trace=def456
```
maria: repro hypothesis: A demotes, schedules async republish using its local snapshot (epoch 41) while B already promoted (epoch 42) and accepted a newer write. republished item arrives later and overwrites newer value because we don't check epoch on republish path.
linda: that fits a race we discussed. republish should be gated by current lease/epoch check. Iirc republish was intended for cold rehydrate, not for demote->handoff flows.
kevin: quick patch idea (pseudo):
```
if republish.epoch != current_prefix_epoch { drop_and_metric++ ; log.trace("republish dropped epoch mismatch", ...) }
else apply_republish()
```
maria: can we add `republish_dropped_epoch` metric and a log with trace id so we can backfill which trace caused it?
sre-oncall: +1 — also suggest an alert: if republish_attempts > 0 and republish_dropped_epoch / republish_attempts < 0.9 for 5m then low-severity alert (we want drops, not successes). if a lot of full-successful republish where epoch mismatch is low, that's suspicious.
aj: for verification, add a unit/canary: loop transfer prefix A->B with concurrent writes and assert final value monotonicity. cheap and catches regressions.
deploy-bot: deploy request queued for kevin/kevin-pr-#1428 to canary.
kevin: I'll open a small PR that drops republish on epoch mismatch and emits metric/log. Will include canary test. PR will also include a short comment in code explaining the property.
linda: one more gotcha: in shared-prefix mode, republish originates from a pool worker that may not have latest epoch mapping. we need a fresh epoch lookup at republish time (or stash the epoch and validate). avoid stale local caches for epoch resolution.
maria: agreed. add a note in the RFC follow-up: "republish path must validate prefix epoch against control-plane at time-of-send or be cancelled by new demote/handshake." I'll write the follow-up doc and a checklist for the canary.
kevin: timeline — small patch -> canary -> observe republish_dropped_epoch metric for 24h -> roll to prod-canary. If stable, roll to prod.
sre-oncall: add dashboard tile: republish_attempts, republish_dropped_epoch, republish_successes, republish_latency. Also correlate with prefix_handoff_rate.
maria: thanks — I'll file the RFC follow-up and include logs/samples. tagging @linda and @kevin for PR reviews. :thumbsup:
